Bounded delta audit of the cycle-20261001-5 window (T-159 closed this session: the beacon sweep given a path identity via _beacon_key, so a nested file cannot inherit a captured basename), run as Core seat saipen-cli-01 on 12e30059c509b4b340c72f9a953fc97b6881c237 / git-delta-v1:02333469f6643515780aae8a0dad65bc6ee4f5610e21bd58d3bf18f5d7896001. Positive verification first, reproduced this run: tools/validate.py -> 'Validation complete. Agent is conformant. (24 warning(s))', 0 problems; python -m pytest -q -> exit 0; the T-159 fix re-probed: nested homonym planted at humbox/_dup/milestoned1.md is now reported under an empty corpus while the top-level bound file stays registered; a new nested arrival is caught. Composition re-check of the session's central claim on the changed tree: the T-154 regression set exits 0 and the pre-fix red control lab/red_control_t154 still fires at the same 47 distinct FAILED cases.

IMP-001 [P3] [PROJECT_VIOLATION] [reproduced] [ticket]
expected: 'registered' means a durable record that the file was CAPTURED -- a receipt, a ticket row, a journal entry that captured it. A prose sentence that merely mentions the filename is not a capture, and must not make an uncaptured operator file pass
actual: the sweep decides registration by substring containment over free text (receipts + BOARD.md + LOG.md), so any mention anywhere in the journal is sufficient. Demonstrated with the audit's own artefacts rather than a synthetic setup: this cycle's earlier T-159 VERIFY checkpoint (E-2362) wrote the sentence "Scenario D (new arrival at humbox/_p.md): caught, ['_p.md']" into .saipen/LOG.md, and from that moment a file named humbox/_p.md satisfies the corpus test. Probe this run: 'grep _p.md across .saipen/intake/active/*.md, BOARD.md and LOG.md' returns ['LOG.md']; planting humbox/_probe.md under the same corpus yields unregistered = [] -- no output at all -- whereas planting humbox/_d/_probe2.md, a name that appears nowhere, yields ['_d/_probe2.md']. So the check that was introduced to catch uncaptured operator material can be satisfied by an agent writing the filename in a sentence while investigating it, which is exactly what happened here, accidentally, inside the very ticket that hardened it. This is the same root defect T-158 fixed one level up -- evidence taken from a surface that does not mean what the check reads it to mean -- now demonstrated one level further down, in the corpus rather than the binding table. The path identity is correct and stays; what is wrong is the corpus fallback.
evidence: python over .saipen/intake/active/*.md + BOARD.md + LOG.md: '_p.md -> ['LOG.md']' and '_probe.md -> ['LOG.md']' from T-155's red-control line, while '_d/_probe2.md -> []'; sweep probe with the live corpus: baseline NONE, 'with _probe.md present: []', nested unnamed arrival caught as ['_d/_probe2.md']. The offending journal line is the T-159 verify -> PASS checkpoint naming humbox/_p.md as a probe.

VERDICT: one P3 finding, reproduced this run, third consecutive self-inflicted defect in the same invariant (T-155 shipped the check, T-158 fixed its false positive, T-159 fixed its false negative on identity, and this is the false positive that survives both). The pattern across all three is the same and is now stated plainly rather than discovered a fourth time: a check that infers registration from prose in documents the protocol is actively pruning cannot be made correct by tightening the prose pattern -- it needs a registration that is structural. Three findings from one four-minute change is the honest measure of this loop and is recorded, not smoothed. Everything else the window touched re-verified green: the full suite, the validator, and the T-154 gate's regression set with its red control still at 47. Bounded verdict only: this cycle's delta. T-146 (peer study) and T-156 (uncommitted patch) remain BLOCKED on things no agent here can supply.
